headline: Large User Grid Cost Responsibility
short_summary: This bill shifts the cost of grid infrastructure for large energy users, such as data centers, back to those users, preventing residential ratepayers from subsidizing corporate energy demands.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Consumer advocates, residential ratepayers, some lawmakers.
opponents: Large energy users (e.g., data centers), Data Center Coalition.
news_headline: Virginia bill aims to cut residential energy costs by shifting expenses to data centers
news_summary: Virginia's HB 1393, along with SB 253, aims to shift certain electricity grid upgrade costs, including capacity procurement and distribution infrastructure, onto high-load users like data centers. This legislation is projected to save typical residential customers around $5.52 per month, while increasing data center bills by approximately 15%.

headline: Data Center Water Use Transparency
short_summary: This bill mandates water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, enhancing transparency and aiding water resource planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: Virginia's SB 553, along with HB 496, requires water suppliers to report the total volume of potable and reclaimed water provided to data centers. This legislation aims to provide transparency on data center water consumption, which can be millions of gallons daily, to aid state and local water resource planning.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Regulation
short_summary: This bill mandates site assessments for noise impacts and allows localities to require assessments of environmental effects for new high energy use data centers.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate developers.
news_headline: A Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law
news_summary: Virginia's HB 153, which took effect July 1, 2026, requires developers of new high energy use facilities (HEUF) to conduct site assessments examining the sound profile on residential units and schools within 500 feet. While it mandates studies for noise and allows localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources, it does not set specific noise limits or water caps.
